verdict.rationale: Alloy documents event-driven automation. Event types can be mapped to a Source Workflow so incoming events are routed automatically for decisioning. Workflows apply policy logic and generate alerts or investigations when thresholds are met, which covers the core 'event triggers action' loop. However, the evidence never shows how users author or configure the rules themselves, and the available actions beyond alerts and investigations are described only at a use-case level. Missing for 10: documentation of the rule-definition interface or syntax, an explicit catalog of triggerable actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: any event can be submitted for additional monitoring by mapping the event type to a Source Workflow. When enabled, Alloy stores the data submitted on events and automatically routes all requests
Monitors transaction events in real time or at scheduled times to detect suspicious activity, apply policy logic, and generate alerts or investigations when thresholds are met.
Alloy's Events API allows you to build a real-time integration for decisioning on suspicious ongoing behavior as soon as it happens.
Alloy supports dozens of use cases like interdicting on transactions, performing step-up after suspicious PII changes, or rejecting unusual login activity.
